context: v1.3.0 Router Gateway design, implementation, debugging and release-readiness

records.claim: Router Gateway is integrated into the existing application as a non-privileged, offline-first configuration-data module. It does not automatically log into or mutate a router.
records.rationale: Router firmware and VPN-client capability vary by vendor/model/firmware; blind router mutation is higher risk and unnecessary for the requested outcome.

records.claim: L2TP/IPsec is the preferred router profile. PPTP is retained only as a legacy compatibility fallback.
records.rationale: Current router-client documentation supports L2TP/PPTP on selected devices, while PPTP is legacy and weaker; the product labels it accordingly.

records.claim: VPN Gate publishes L2TP/IPsec credentials username=vpn, password=vpn, IPsec PSK=vpn and recommends numeric IP use when hostname access is filtered.
VPNBook PPTP snapshot observed 2026-09-29 used servers pl134.vpnbook.com, pl140.vpnbook.com, ca225.vpnbook.com, username vpnbook and rotating password ngzc6a8.
records.limitation: Password rotates; bundled snapshot is labeled rotating and Refresh attempts best-effort update.

records.claim: Direct live provider fetch was not reliable from both hosts during development.
evidence: Linux curl to VPN Gate returned TLS wrong-version-number; Windows Invoke-WebRequest probe timed out.
records.rootCause: Environment/filtering/transport behavior made provider websites unreliable as a sole runtime dependency.
records.prevention: Offline-first bundled manifest + cache + repository refresh; upstream refresh failure is non-fatal.

records.claim: First Windows Router Gateway compile exposed malformed JSON string mutation and then a missing System.IO namespace.
records.rootCause: Initial implementation defect in C# refresh helper and imports.
records.prevention: Replaced text mutation with JsonNode object mutation; added System.IO; full dotnet build required.

records.claim: Live UI endpoint test initially classified VPNBook as reachable because DNS resolved it to private 10.10.34.35 and TCP/1723 answered.
records.rootCause: Reachability heuristic trusted DNS output without rejecting private/reserved interception addresses.
records.prevention: Windows IsPublicEndpointAddress guard and Linux ipaddress.is_global guard; private/reserved resolutions now fail closed as DNS intercepted/private.
regression: Final WPF UI smoke: Unverified · DNS intercepted/private address 10.10.34.35

records.claim: Linux deployment-copy contract initially failed after partial sync because protected backend source was stale.
records.rootCause: Deployment copy drift: linux/system/install_system.sh did not match canonical repo.
records.prevention: Canonical backend source synchronized for parity without mutating the installed protected backend.
regression: Linux contract PASS after parity sync

records.claim: Final Windows payload gate passed service self-test, 678-file manifest rebuild, full Windows regression contract and Router Gateway inclusion.
Linux runtime smoke loaded 8 profiles, generated required L2TP fields, rejected synthetic private DNS, and reached VPN Gate numeric endpoint 219.100.37.213 via TCP/443.
records.limitation: TCP/443 is an informational reachability heuristic, not an L2TP/IPsec authentication handshake.

records.claim: Linux release ZIP reproduced byte-identically on Windows and Linux.
A complete authenticated L2TP/IPsec or PPTP tunnel handshake on a physical router was not performed in this change set.
records.rationale: The requested product output is modem/router configuration data. Forcing a live router/host tunnel would mutate network state and requires a specific compatible router model/firmware.
records.consequence: Endpoint reachability and configuration generation are validated; exact router-model E2E remains model-dependent.
